question: As recorded, not shared. The record sets P-1153's MCI-to-AD iAUC in baseline-MCI ADNI (0.787) against P-1154's AUC for direct CN-to-AD conversion in ADNI 'cognitively normal' adults (0.994); those are different baseline populations and endpoints. Both papers do print one shared question: prediction of progression from normal cognition to MCI from FDG-PET plus clinical and cognitive covariates, with PET the shared channel. P-1153 answers it in HABS NC (n = 274, 22 progressors); P-1154 answers it with its 'MCI as first event' outcome in ADNI CN (n = 1,136). Whether the population behind P-1154's CN label is cognitively normal is in doubt on its own pages. It defines CN as MMSE >= 24 and CDR 0, yet reports a stratum 'with MCI at baseline (MMSE 20-23)' and a mean baseline MMSE of 21.0 in its direct-converter pathway. Its Table 4 counts 514 of 1,136 (45.4%) with MCI as first event within 12 months, against 8.0% progressors over about five years in HABS.
metric: AUC-type discrimination in both. P-1153 reports the integrated time-dependent AUC of a Cox model over follow-up; P-1154 reports fixed-horizon ROC AUCs (12, 24, 36 months) from a multinomial pathway model. The construction differs; both are AUCs for the same binary transition.

figures.P-1153: HABS NC, NC to MCI: Model 1 (age, gender, education, APOE4, PACC + FDG SUVR) iAUC 0.817, printed 95% CI 0.692-0.909; Model 2 (+ DL score) 0.902 (0.751-0.951); 22 progressors of 274, follow-up IQR 4.5-5.2 years. For context, the recorded figure is ADNI MCI to AD, Model 2, 0.787 (0.766-0.811).
figures.P-1154: MCI as first event: AUC 0.686 (12 m, 514 events), 0.643 (24 m, 520), 0.680 (36 m, 525). The column is headed 'AUC (95 % CI)' but no interval is printed. Hanley-McNeil over the whole cohort (n2 = 1,136 - events): 0.686, Q1 = 0.5221, Q2 = 0.5582, SE = 0.0159, CI [0.655, 0.717]; 0.643, SE = 0.0165, CI [0.611, 0.675]; 0.680, SE = 0.0159, CI [0.649, 0.711]. If only a 20% temporal test split were scored, SE rises to about 0.036 and the 12-month CI is about [0.616, 0.756]. The recorded figure is direct AD conversion, 0.999/0.994/0.994.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure reconciles the shared question. P-1153 prints no fixed-horizon AUC for HABS, and P-1154 prints no iAUC, so no figure is reported under the other's horizon or metric construction. For the recorded pair, the papers share no population stratum: P-1153's ADNI and J-ADNI strata are MCI at baseline, and P-1154 has no MCI-to-AD figure for a baseline-MCI group.
performance_validity: The figures compared on the shared question (0.817/0.902 and 0.64-0.69) are far below 0.97. P-1154's direct-conversion AUCs (0.994-0.999) are near ceiling on internal ADNI cross-validation with no external cohort. The sample (1,136) is not small, so the Section 3.5 exclusion as written does not apply. Those near-ceiling figures, obtained with baseline cognition among the predictors, add to the doubt about what P-1154's CN label contains.

candidate_explanations.difference: Population behind the label: P-1154's 'cognitively normal' cohort includes participants it describes as having MCI at baseline, and its progression base rate is far higher than HABS's.
candidate_explanations.quote: Among participants with MCI at baseline (MMSE 20–23), low FDG metabolism resulted in six-fold higher risk

candidate_explanations.difference: Metric construction: Cox-model iAUC integrated over follow-up, against fixed-horizon ROC AUC from a multinomial pathway model.
candidate_explanations.quote: the added prognostic value of DL output over clinical features and SUVR was assessed by calculating the integrated area under the time-dependent ROC curves (iAUC) for Cox regression models

candidate_explanations.difference: Predictors: P-1153 uses age, gender, education, APOE4, PACC and FDG SUVR (posterior cingulate/precuneus, pons reference); P-1154 uses an FDG MetaROI z-score 'supplemented by baseline cognitive measures when appropriate'.
candidate_explanations.quote: Pathway prediction modeling utilized multinomial logistic regres­sion with brain glucose metabolism as the primary predictor, supple­mented by baseline cognitive measures when appropriate.

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort and event count: HABS community volunteers with 22 progressors, against ADNI with more than 500 MCI-first events.
candidate_explanations.quote: the HABS NC set was divided into two groups based on the DL output median (low-risk: DL output < the median, high-risk: DL output ≥ the median) due to the small number of progressors (Table 1).

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation: P-1153's Cox models are fitted within HABS, with resampling used for the model comparison; P-1154 uses temporal and subject-grouped cross-validation within ADNI.
candidate_explanations.quote: Cross-validation method utilized temporal splitting to prevent opti­mistic bias, training models on earlier ADNI enrollment cohorts and validating on later cohorts.

reason: The recorded gap (0.787 against 0.994) sets MCI-to-AD prognosis in baseline MCI against direct CN-to-AD conversion in CN adults, so as recorded it fails condition 1. On the question both papers do print, CN to MCI with FDG-PET, the figures separate beyond uncertainty with no matched figure. HABS gives 0.817 (0.692-0.909) and 0.902 (0.751-0.951); ADNI gives 0.686/0.643/0.680, with derived intervals of about +/-0.03, so the separation holds both ways, though narrowly against Model 1 (0.686 against a lower bound of 0.692). The pair is borderline because condition 1 then rests on P-1154's cohort being cognitively normal, and P-1154's own pages contradict that: it reports an 'MCI at baseline (MMSE 20-23)' stratum, a direct-converter mean MMSE of 21.0 and 45% reaching MCI within 12 months. The candidate explanations are not shown to be sufficient.
